record.original_question: For each fixed integer t>1, is there a polynomial-time algorithm that, given a graph G of treewidth at most t, determines the value of the list packing number χ⋆ℓ(G)?

evidence.quote: Problem 2.11 (Question 7.3 in [3]) Fix t > 1. Is the problem of determining the value of χ⋆ ℓ(G)or χ• ℓ(G), given a graph G of treewidth at most t as input, in P?

artifact.self_contained_problem:
Let G=(V,E) be a finite simple graph. A list assignment for G is a function L that assigns to every vertex v∈V a finite set L(v) of colors. A proper L-coloring of G is a function c: V→⋃_v L(v) such that c(v)∈L(v) for every v∈V and c(u)≠c(v) whenever uv∈E. 

For an integer k≥1, a k-fold L-packing of G is a sequence (c_1,c_2,…,c_k) of proper L-colorings of G with the additional property that, for every vertex v∈V, the colors c_1(v),c_2(v),…,c_k(v) are pairwise distinct (so they form a k-subset of L(v)). The list packing number χ⋆_ℓ(G) is defined as the smallest integer k such that, for every list assignment L with |L(v)|=k for all v∈V, there exists a k-fold L-packing of G.

The treewidth of G is defined in the usual way via tree decompositions: it is the minimum, over all tree decompositions (T,{X_t}_{t∈V(T)}) of G, of (max_t |X_t|)−1.

Question. Fix an integer t>1. Is there a polynomial-time algorithm that, given as input a graph G with treewidth at most t, computes the exact value of the list packing number χ⋆_ℓ(G)?
artifact.status_search_result: List packing was introduced recently (Cambie et al.) and the list packing number χ⋆_ℓ has been studied for several graph classes, but no published result establishes a polynomial-time algorithm to compute χ⋆_ℓ(G) on graphs of bounded treewidth. The question is explicitly posed as an open problem in recent workshop problem collections, and recent literature on list packing (e.g., works by Cambie and Cames van Batenburg) treats algorithmic complexity on bounded-treewidth inputs as unresolved.

status_evidence.title: A Short Proof that the List Packing Number of any Graph is Well Defined
status_evidence.snippet: List packing number χ⋆_ℓ(G) is the least k such that any k-list assignment admits k disjoint proper L-colorings.
status_evidence.claim: Establishes the definition and finiteness of χ⋆_ℓ(G) without addressing complexity on bounded-treewidth graphs.

status_evidence.title: Fractional List Packing for Layered Graphs
status_evidence.snippet: Bounds on the fractional list packing number χ•_ℓ for various graph classes.
status_evidence.claim: Recent work focuses on bounds rather than polynomial-time exact computation on bounded-treewidth graphs.

status_evidence.title: List packing number of bounded degree graphs
status_evidence.snippet: Studies list packing number for bounded-degree graphs.
status_evidence.claim: Bounded-treewidth algorithmic question is not addressed/resolved in this line of work.
